messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: high error rate and elevated OOMs on inference-gpu-pool. Autoscaler generated many rapid scale events. See incident console: https://redwood.incidents/1785554321 ; runbook: /runbooks/autoscale-brownout.md

jess: i'm oncall, grabbing it now. can someone paste the autoscaler timeline?

omar: pulling metrics — looks like multiple scale cycles: 8 -> 2 -> 14 -> 3 within ~9 minutes. pods evicted mid-warmup, causing heavy memory churn.

lee: logs from one crashed pod (`svc-gen-3-7d9b`) show repeated allocation failures and then SIGKILL. snippet:
```
2026-03-15T05:42:10Z model-worker[pid]: Allocating 4.8GB tensors
2026-03-15T05:42:11Z model-worker[pid]: RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 3.6 GiB
2026-03-15T05:42:11Z kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 16234 (python) score 987 or sacrifice child
```

tasha: paging customers now — CS alerted for impacted accounts. early impact: about 12% error rate for APAC and EU routes; latency up to 2.5s.

jess: immediate actions: 1) set autoscaler pause 2) set minReplicas=current to prevent scale-downs 3) shift heavy routes to quantized fallback 4) cordon suspicious nodes. who can run pause?

omar: running `redwood infra autoscaler pause --cluster inference-prod --reason "rapid scale thrash -> OOMs"`. Also pinning `minReplicas=14` for gpu-pool-2.

devops-bot: autoscaler paused by omar. minReplicas set to 14 for gpu-pool-2.

lee: observed driver errors before OOM: `NVRM: Xid 79` repeated about 30s prior. opening infra-driver ticket.

jess: good catch. tasha, can you flip traffic to fallback variant for the most-used routes? we need to reduce memory footprint quickly.

tasha: initiating routing override: `traffic-rule apply --route /v1/chat --model text-gen-fallback-quant --weight 100%` — doing canary then full.

cs-alert: customer banner posted: "Degraded inference for some customers — mitigation in progress. ETA next update 30m." Top affected customers notified.

omar: after traffic shift OOMs decreased but we still see crashloops for pods that were previously evicted. i'm cordoning node gpu-07 and draining. commands: `kubectl cordon gpu-07` then `kubectl drain gpu-07 --force --ignore-daemonsets`

lee: kernel logs from gpu-07 show GPU driver resets and repeated Xid errors. suspect combined driver + heavy memory fragmentation.

jess: we're keeping autoscaler paused until we confirm stable for 10m. propose increasing warm pool by 30% for this class of model. also adjust autoscaler cooldown to 6m.

omar: applied warm-pool increase. updated autoscaler config: `--cooldown 360s --stabilization-window 360s`. pushed config; rolling update in progress.

lee: confirming that pods rescheduled to healthy nodes are stable. crashloop count down from 11 -> 2 in last 15m. OOM tracebacks now rare.

tasha: CS reporting errors down to 3% and latency back to ~600-700ms for most customers. keeping banner live while we monitor.

jess: handoff plan: i'll stay active to finalize timeline and capture root cause notes. omar, you own remediation tasks (driver ticket + model memory estimate fixes). lee, follow kernel/driver investigation. tasha continues customer comms.

omar: filing follow-ups: 1) add pre-deploy memory estimator check for new model variants 2) extend warm pool in prod by default for >6GB models 3) bump autoscaler stabilization default to 5m 4) coordinate driver upgrade with infra team.

devops-bot: runbook step completed: traffic fallback applied; warm pool adjusted.

jess: quick post-incident checklist for the postmortem: timeline, root cause (aggressive autoscaler + underestimated model RAM + driver resets), mitigation steps, action owners, and detection improvements (watch for Xid spikes).

lee: i collected dmesg/gpu logs and attached ticket id INFRA-2321 to the driver team. recommending patch testing in staging before roll.

tasha: CS will send final update in 1h and notify enterprise accounts directly. severity set to Sev2 -> will downgrade when errors <1% for 30m.

omar: i'll unpause autoscaler only after we see 15m of stable metrics post-cooldown change.

jess: thanks all — handoff to oncall tomorrow is scheduled. creating incident doc now and marking postmortem required. :white_check_mark:
